title: Dot Halftone
description: Any image recreated as a field of dots on one canvas, sized by ink coverage, morphing between images with a radial implode and explode wave.

loop.script: click[1] → wait → click[2] → wait → click[3] → wait → click[0] → wait

props.name: src
props.description: The image to recreate as dots (same origin, CORS or a data URL). Changing it plays the morph. Images on white or transparent backgrounds work best: white is keyed out.

props.name: gradient
props.description: A top-to-bottom pair of hex colors that recolors the dots; without it each dot takes the image's ink color.

props.name: accent
props.description: Color of the corner dot clusters.

props.name: alt
props.description: Describes the picture; without it the halftone is decorative (aria-hidden).

props.name: fallback
props.description: Replaces the static picture shown before the first frame (and in the server render).

a11y: With alt it is role="img" with that name; without it the whole picture is decorative. The corner clusters and the dotted backdrop are always aria-hidden.
Reduced motion: the dots are drawn at once, without the morph.
Before the dots are drawn (and in the server render) the image shows through a CSS dot screen, so the picture reads without JavaScript.
usage: <DotHalftone src="/rocket.png" gradient={["#ff6ea6", "#7b2ff7"]} alt="A rocket drawn in dots" className="max-w-sm" />
docs:
Installed `DotHalftone` in `components/ui/`, plus the `render-loop` helper in `lib/`. Render `<DotHalftone src="/rocket.png" alt="A rocket drawn in dots" className="max-w-sm" />`; it is square and as wide as its container by default, so size it with `className`. Change `src` to play the morph.

The dots and the corner clusters draw 24 px outside the box and the dotted backdrop 40 px outside it, so leave room around it. Colors: `gradient` recolors the dots, `--dot-halftone-accent` the corner clusters and `--dot-halftone-grid` the dotted backdrop. Drawing pauses off screen and in hidden tabs; under reduced motion the dots appear without the morph.
